**Needs changes before merge.** One pinning test failed in the quick gate of this review. The production code has no finding.

This is a SAFETY-tier review, because the PR changes the route of a geometry import. It was built and tested locally on macOS (arm64), merged with `upstream/main` at `75e74a9cb`. No GitHub runner was used.

## What looks good

- The file path is one argument of the child. No shell runs. The search of `PATH` ignores each entry that is not absolute.
- The private folder is made with mode `0700`, and `create` refuses a name that exists. A `Drop` guard removes it.
- The child writes to files, not to pipes. The time limit, the 16 MiB capture limit and the STEP size limit are read in one loop.
- `--allow-errors` is never given. A report that is not JSON refuses the part.
- `QUALIFIED` is empty, so no shipped import reaches the runner. Each native extension is refused by name, as IGES was.
- The stated path is used alone. A wrong path does not fall back to `PATH`.
- No `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!()` is in the new production code. Each new module has a provenance line. Each file is below 400 lines.
- No `Cargo.toml`, `build.rs`, `.github/`, `scripts/`, snapshot PNG, golden or `CHANGELOG.md` changed. The decision file is `docs/decisions/1873-cadmpeg-runner.md`.
- The body has the `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #1873`. The commit subject is conventional.
- The change in `crates/ui` (`state_prefs.rs`) changes no control and no layout. Screenshots are not necessary.
- I read the stand-in program `testdata/stubs/cadmpeg_stub.sh` before the tests ran. It writes only below the folder of its link.

## Results merged with main (local)

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | 45 steps, 44 ok, **1 failed** |
| `app suites: cadmpeg_import` in that gate | **12 passed, 1 failed** |
| `cadmpeg_import`, 3 later runs with less load | 13 passed each |
| `app suites: view_prefs`, `import_bytes`, the STEP import suites, `lib` | ok |
| `ui suites: lib` (with `prefs_door::a_pick_keeps_the_stated_cadmpeg_path`) and the 15 other ui suites | ok |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The failure text from the gate:

```
---- stub::a_hung_program_is_stopped_at_the_time_limit_and_its_folder_removed stdout ----
thread '...' panicked at crates/app/tests/cadmpeg_import.rs:220:9:
cadmpeg did not finish `--version` within 400ms and was stopped; nothing was imported
test result: FAILED. 12 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 1.13s
```

A second build ran on this machine at the same time. That is the usual condition of the batch gate and of a pool machine.

## Mutations (run by the reviewer)

| Guard removed | Expected red test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| unqualified refusal in `checked_budget` (`import_model.rs:163`) | `unqualified_native_extensions_are_refused_by_name` | red |
| `check` exit status (`cadmpeg/mod.rs:189`) | `stub::a_failed_check_is_refused_and_nothing_is_converted` | red |
| `--reject-lossy=export` replaced by `--allow-errors` (`cadmpeg/mod.rs:238`) | `stub::a_converted_part_imports_through_the_step_importer` | red |
| `stop(&mut child)` at a limit (`cadmpeg/run.rs:141`) | `stub::a_hung_program_is_stopped_...` | **green on macOS** |

All files were restored after the runs, and the suite was green again (13 passed). No golden moved, so there was no golden to read.

## Requested before merge

1. `crates/app/tests/cadmpeg_import.rs:216` - the test sets `settings.timeout` to 400 ms. `cadmpeg/mod.rs:145` applies the same limit to the `--version` question (`settings.timeout.min(PROBE_TIMEOUT)`). On a loaded machine the start of the shell stand-in takes more than 400 ms. Then the run stops at `--version`, and the assertion for `check` at line 220 fails. This test goes into the batch gate, and a red post-merge run opens a `main is red` issue. Make the test independent of the machine load. For example, use a limit of 2 s or 3 s: the stand-in sleeps for 30 s, so the 15 s ceiling of the test still proves the stop.
2. `crates/app/tests/cadmpeg_import.rs:223` - the check that the child is gone is `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` only. On macOS the removal of `stop(&mut child)` stays green. The mutation table of the body says that this test is red. Add a check that operates on each Unix (for example `kill -0 <pid>` through `std::process::Command`, and require a status that is not zero). Alternatively, say in the body that this pin is for Linux only.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- `check` passes with exit status 0 and a JSON report that has no `findings` list (`{}` or `[]`). Decision 2 accepts this, because the exit status is the documented contract. #1875 can make this more strict when a real report is available.
- The limits apply to the two capture files and to `converted.step`. A different file that the child writes into the private folder has only the time limit. The folder is removed in each case.
- `crates/ui/src/state_prefs.rs:68` reads the preferences file again at each save. This is correct while no control sets the path. #1876 replaces it.
- When #1875 adds a format, `Settings::from_prefs` reads the preferences file of the user in each import, also in a headless test. A test of that path must give its own `Settings`.
- This is a `feat` PR. It merges at the next cut.
- The decision about the `formats --json` probe (decision 1) stays with the maintainer.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: both requested test changes from the latest review.

1. The hung-child test now uses a three-second timeout. The stub delays its version reply by one second. This pins the probe budget without machine load. Restoring 400 ms makes the test fail at `--version`. Restoring three seconds makes it pass.
2. The test now uses `kill -0` on every Unix platform to check that the child exited. Removing `stop(&mut child)` makes it fail on macOS with `process 23075 still runs`. Restoring the call makes it pass.

Both findings are pinned by `stub::a_hung_program_is_stopped_at_the_time_limit_and_its_folder_removed`. The full `cadmpeg_import` suite passes all 13 tests. Production code is unchanged.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: RED, 42 of 44 steps passed. All app checks passed. The UI test `headless_run_succeeds` failed because Metal found no graphics adapter. The UI test `headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero` returned 1. These UI checks are unchanged.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN. The checks ran with the compile cache disabled because the shared cache was unavailable.

New head: `46c5538467e15a069d802e667dd54fe90efdd239`.

Please re-review this head.

**Needs changes before merge.** Both findings from the previous review are resolved. Two required extra suites fail in the trial merge.

This is a SAFETY-tier review because the PR changes geometry import routing. All checks ran locally on macOS arm64. The trial merge uses `upstream/main` at `a4e5a68abfc17e9d46bb8e48015935cb9e2de6a7`. No GitHub runner ran. I checked the laws in that main revision.

## What looks good

- The child receives file paths as separate arguments. No shell reads them.
- The stated program path takes precedence. The search ignores relative PATH entries.
- The private folder, time limit, capture limit, STEP size limit and refusal paths have tests.
- The qualified-extension table stays empty. No shipped native import reaches the converter yet.
- The preferences retain the converter path. The UI change affects persistence only; no control or layout changes. Before/after screenshots do not apply.
- No dependency, process file, snapshot PNG or golden changes. There are no moved goldens to check.
- The body names the unsupported `formats --json` probe and records the decision. Real cadmpeg, Windows and wasm32 remain untested.

## Earlier findings

1. The timeout is now three seconds. The version reply has a one-second delay. Restoring 400 ms makes the test fail at `--version`.
2. The child-exit assertion now runs on every Unix platform. Omitting the stop makes the test fail on macOS with `process 51957 still runs`.

Both fixes pass with the original code restored.

## Results merged with main (local)

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: **43 steps passed, 2 failed**. Both crate builds passed.

The UI library has 1240 passed, 1 failed and 7 ignored tests. The failure is `egui_app::tests::headless_run_succeeds`:

```
egui headless run failed: no graphics adapter
metal found no adapters
```

The UI `shell` suite has 20 passed and 1 failed test. `headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero` returns 1 instead of 0. These unchanged rendering checks cannot pass with the adapter unavailable. They are an environment limitation, separate from the two findings below.

`cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.

The first cache-enabled compilation stopped making progress. I stopped it and ran the checks with `RUSTC_WRAPPER=` and the optional gate cache disabled.

## Extra suites run

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-kernel --test step_agreement` | 18 passed, **1 failed** |
| `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-kernel --test step_import` | 4 passed |
| `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-kernel --test machining_mesh` | 7 passed |
| `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-app --test feature_edge_g1_join` | 4 passed, **1 failed** |

The three kernel targets were first selected in one cargo command. Cargo stopped after `step_agreement` failed. I then ran `step_import` separately.

The only changed test-data file is `testdata/stubs/cadmpeg_stub.sh`. A source search finds its reader in `cadmpeg_import` only. That suite passed all 13 tests in the gate and after the mutations. No new STEP fixture needs a row in this PR.

## Mutations run by the reviewer

| Mutation | Pin | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Omit the limit-path `stop(&mut child)` | `stub::a_hung_program_is_stopped_at_the_time_limit_and_its_folder_removed` | RED: child still runs |
| Ignore the `check` exit status | `stub::a_failed_check_is_refused_and_nothing_is_converted` | RED: unsafe acceptance reaches `must refuse` |
| Restore the 400 ms timeout | `stub::a_hung_program_is_stopped_at_the_time_limit_and_its_folder_removed` | RED: version probe times out |

All temporary edits were restored. The complete `cadmpeg_import` suite then passed: **13 passed, 0 failed**. `git status --short` is empty.

## Requested before merge

These are failures of the required trial-merge checks. The fixture entered upstream main in commit `371813425`. This PR does not change that fixture or the two failing test sources. They are not new defects in the cadmpeg code. The explicit extra-suite rule still makes them blockers.

1. `crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement.rs:466` — `step_files_agree_or_refuse_by_name` fails because `bar_cross_holes.step` has no row. Add its measured verdict and per-file test upstream, then repeat this review against the corrected main. Do not remove the fixture check.

   ```
   assertion `left == right` failed: a fixture has no row, or a row has no fixture - re-triage
   ```

2. `crates/app/tests/feature_edge_g1_join.rs:94` — the fixture-wide edge check finds 116 tangent-edge pairs that pick separately in `bar_cross_holes.step`. Correct the upstream edge behavior and repeat this required suite. Do not exclude the fixture to clear the test.

   ```
   tangent pieces of one edge pick apart: [
       "bar_cross_holes.step: 116 pairs, first (164185, 164857)",
   ]
   ```

The trial merge is clean, but these required checks are red. Keep `needs-rework` and the draft state. No new production-code finding applies to the cadmpeg change. This feature still follows the next-cut merge rule.
